additional_concerns: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1 preserve ultimate responsibility despite outsourcing, but supply no complete test of effective retention or supervisory discharge. Practical authority and conduct may be evidence; neither is an established sufficient condition.

Defective records can establish failure of a substantive duty without alone establishing loss of ultimate accountability. Conversely, retained accountability does not establish sound operations or proper records.
The applicable Part A Appendix factors are absent. Supply that Appendix and its applicability basis before deriving a supervisory standard; no external dependency ID is supplied.

The register provisions permit an appointed register keeper while retaining the specified maintenance duty. They do not establish that appointment transfers the Product Provider's ultimate responsibility.

Intermediary paragraph 13 preserves responsibility for overall operation within its stated issuance and intended dealing/advising scope. Applying it to this Product Provider requires facts establishing that scope.

Paragraph 15 concerns requested third-party audit or verification of three specified subjects; paragraph 16 concerns a requested legal opinion supporting the application. Neither supplies an accountability safe harbour.
No executable meaning or actual arrangement facts are supplied. Retrieval success and the unsupported LegalRuleML result establish neither legal sufficiency nor satisfaction of this requirement.
